verses.text: From Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and a brother of James. To those who are called, who are loved and made holy by God the Father, and kept safe for Jesus Christ:
May you have more and more mercy, peace, and love.
Dear friends, I really wanted to write to you about the salvation we all share. But I felt I had to write and urge you to fight hard for the faith that God gave to his holy people once and for all.

Some people have sneaked in among you without being noticed. Long ago it was written that they would be judged. They are ungodly people. They turn the grace of our God into an excuse for shameful living, and they reject Jesus Christ, our only Master and Lord.
You already know all this, but I want to remind you. The Lord saved his people out of the land of Egypt, but later he destroyed those who did not believe.
And there were angels who did not stay in their place of power, but left their own home. God has kept them in chains that last forever, in darkness, waiting for the judgment on the great day.

In the same way, Sodom and Gomorrah and the towns around them gave themselves to sexual sin and chased unnatural desires. They are shown as an example of those who suffer the punishment of fire that lasts forever.
In the same way, these people follow their dreams. They make their bodies dirty with sin, reject authority, and say evil things about heavenly beings.
But even Michael, the chief angel, when he was arguing with the devil about the body of Moses, did not dare to accuse him with insulting words. He only said, "May the Lord rebuke you!"
But these people speak evil of things they do not understand. And the things they do understand by instinct, like animals without reason, are the very things that destroy them.
How terrible it will be for them! They have followed the way of Cain. They have rushed into Balaam's mistake for money. And they have been destroyed like Korah in his rebellion.

These people are like hidden rocks at your love feasts, where they eat with you without shame. They are shepherds who only feed themselves. They are clouds without water, blown along by the wind. They are trees in autumn without fruit, dead twice over, pulled up by the roots.
They are wild waves of the sea, foaming up their own shame. They are wandering stars, and the deepest darkness has been kept for them forever.
Enoch, who lived seven generations after Adam, spoke as a prophet about these people. He said, "Look, the Lord is coming with many thousands of his holy ones,

to judge everyone, and to show all the ungodly people how wrong they are. He will judge them for all the ungodly things they have done in ungodly ways, and for all the harsh words ungodly sinners have spoken against him."
These people grumble and complain. They follow their own wrong desires. They boast about themselves, and they flatter others to get what they want.
But you, dear friends, remember the words spoken earlier by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ.
They told you, "In the last times there will be people who mock, and who follow their own ungodly desires."
These are the people who divide you. They follow their natural desires and do not have the Spirit.
But you, dear friends, keep building yourselves up in your most holy faith, and pray in the Holy Spirit.
Keep yourselves in God's love, as you wait for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ to bring you to life that lasts forever.
Be kind to those who have doubts.
Save others by pulling them out of the fire. Show mercy to others, but be careful, and hate even the clothes that are stained by sin.
Now to him who is able to keep you from falling, and to bring you without fault and with great joy into his glorious presence,
to the only God our Saviour, through Jesus Christ our Lord, be glory, greatness, power, and authority, before all time, now, and forever. Amen.
